summary: The spec facts check out against the repository, and the design follows the PM decisions and the AGENTS.md hashing policy: a Git blob id comparison, no new hash field, no manifest, and no task makes a live run, a deploy, or a gcloud write. The zero-decision check fails on two open choices: the bind step container image with its git dependency, and the Phase 2 test file location. Criteria 6, 14, and 15 also lack the automated test that section 5 of the spec promises. Verdict: fail.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] spec.md section 3, plan.md task 1.2: The spec names no container image for the bind step and no way for the step to get git. Rationale: The step must fetch the commit and read blob ids with git; every bash step of the six files runs on node:22-slim, an image without git, and those steps install curl with apt-get; Green must pick the image and the install, so a dependency choice stays open and the zero-decision check fails.

F2 [Blocker] spec.md section 5 (Phase 2 criteria), plan.md task 2.1: The Phase 2 test file location stays open. Rationale: The spec says `in the same test file or a new file next to it`, and task 2.1 names no test file; a file location that the plan leaves to the implementer is a design choice, and the zero-decision check fails.
nonblocking_findings: F3 [Major] spec.md section 5, plan.md tasks 1.1, 1.4, 2.1, 2.4: Criteria 6, 14, and 15 hold no automated test, against the claim of section 5 that each criterion has one. Rationale: Task 1.1 covers criteria 1 to 5 and task 2.1 covers 8 to 13; the phase checks read `git diff --stat`, which shows file names only, so a new hash field inside a changed file stays hidden; a person reads the diff, so the evidence is person-checked, not automated.

F4 [Major] spec.md section 2, section 3a, FR-10: The sales traffic submit source stays unreconciled. Rationale: Section 3a says the sales upload is the release archive, and FR-10 exists for that model; the runbook rule for every traffic file (docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md line 18) says a person submits `.` from the repository root, and that upload already holds scripts/ci; no task changes the rule, so the operator cannot tell which source to submit, and the path of the release-source.json exception stays unnamed.

F5 [Nit] spec.md section 1: The sentence `Neither step reads the uploaded files` is imprecise. Rationale: verify-curriculum-backup runs node apps/sales-advantage/scripts/verify-sales-release-inputs.mjs from the upload; FR-1 orders the bind step before it anyway, so the build does not change.

F6 [Nit] spec.md section 2: The root .gcloudignore re-includes six apps, not seven. Rationale: The file re-includes accounting, codecamp-advantage, marketing, sales-advantage, accounts, and www-reading-advantage; the load-bearing claim that scripts/ stays unexcluded holds.

F7 [Nit] plan.md tasks 1.3 and 2.3: The runbook updates carry no clean-tree rule. Rationale: Q6 stops the build on any untracked file; the five working-tree uploads hold untracked files that .gcloudignore does not exclude; one runbook line that says start from a clean checkout closes the gap.

paraphrase.proposes: This track binds the uploaded source of six manual traffic builds to the release commit before any step that reads that source. A new first step bind-release-source refuses a _RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA that is not 40 lowercase hex characters, fetches that commit from GitHub, and compares the Git blob id of each uploaded file, except release-source.json, with the blob id of the same path in the commit. A file that differs, or is missing from the commit, stops the build. Phase 1 covers sales-advantage and creates the shared script scripts/ci/verify-traffic-source.sh; Phase 2 adds the same step to accounts, accounting, codecamp-advantage, marketing, and primary-advantage. The change adds no hash field and no manifest, and no task makes a live run, a deploy, or a gcloud write.
paraphrase.current_system: A person starts each cloudbuild-traffic.yaml by hand, on Daniel's word, and uploads a source tree. The push path binds its build: cd-apps.yml passes the pushed commit as _RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA, and line 11 of apps/sales-advantage/cloudbuild.yaml runs release-source-manifest.mjs verify against a SHA-256 manifest. The traffic files hold no binding: sales uses the SHA only as a label in two steps, and the other five files never mention it. The first source-reading step of each file runs pnpm install and a migrate command from the upload, so a wrong tree can change the production schema. The sales upload is the release archive that create-sales-release-archive.sh builds from a fixed path list; the other five uploads come from the repository root through the root .gcloudignore.
